transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… mainly sleep. It’s been really unreliable. I can be exhausted when I get into bed, but then I just lie there thinking about forecasts and stuff with my team. And if I wake up around 3 or 4, my brain just doesn’t really shut off again.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of your life?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not just one thing. Most days it jumps around—launch numbers, whether someone on my team might leave, the mortgage, client renewals. Small delays start to feel like they could turn into something much bigger.
When you start worrying, does it feel hard to stop or control the worry?

Yeah. I mean, I try to tell myself, “Brenda, you already made the plan, just let it go.” But then a few minutes later I’m back in it again… one worry gets settled and then a few more show up. It’s hard to shut down.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight or wound up?
Yeah… pretty often. I feel kind of wound up most of the time, even when I’m just home eating dinner. My shoulders especially stay tight, like I can’t really get them to relax.
Has this pattern of excessive worry been present more days than not for at least six months?
Yeah… more than six months. It’s been building since the sales division reorganization, so… about thirteen months now.
When you can’t fall back asleep, is it usually because your mind is busy with worry?
Yes. Usually it’s work stuff… forecasts, team issues. I’ll be exhausted, but my mind just keeps going, and if I wake up at 3 or 4, I can’t really get it to power down again.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know… not really depressed, I guess. Maybe just worn out. I haven’t really thought of it as feeling “down.”
Do you feel these symptoms began because of the sales division reorganization?
I think so, yeah. It’s… that’s when it started building, after the reorganization. About thirteen months ago.
Do you feel your worry is mostly about the sales division reorganization and its consequences?

Mostly, yes… but it’s not only that. My mind kind of jumps around — launch numbers, someone on my team maybe leaving, client renewals, the mortgage. It feels like every small delay could become a big problem.
Outside of work, do you still find yourself worrying a lot about other parts of your life?

Yeah… I do. It’s not just work. I’ll start with the launch numbers, then I’m thinking someone on my team might quit, then it’s the mortgage or a client renewal. It’s like any small delay feels like it could turn into something bigger.
Do you often have trouble concentrating because of the worry?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I get distracted sometimes, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s because of the worry.
Do you get tired easily during the day?
I don’t know… not especially, I guess. Some days I feel worn out, but I haven’t really noticed if I get tired easily during the day.
When you have trouble sleeping, do you find yourself worrying specifically about not being able to sleep?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s more that I’ll go to bed completely exhausted, and then I’m just lying there thinking through forecasts or team stuff. And if I wake up at like 3 or 4, I start worrying that I won’t get back to sleep, and then my brain just won’t shut off.
On nights when you are not feeling especially worried, do you still have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Not as much, I don’t think. It’s usually when my mind gets stuck on work stuff—forecasts, team issues. I’ll be exhausted, but I can’t settle down, and if I wake up around 3 or 4, it’s hard to shut my brain off again.
Does your level of worry feel bigger than the situation really calls for?

Yeah… probably. I mean, it feels justified in the moment, but then I’ll realize I’m going from launch numbers to someone maybe quitting to the mortgage or some client renewal, like every little delay is going to become a huge problem. So… yes, I guess it can feel bigger than it should.
Do you often feel restless, like you can’t really settle down?

Yeah… pretty often. I feel kind of wound up most of the time, like I can’t fully switch off. Even at home, just having dinner, it can feel like I’m still in a pipeline review. My shoulders are tight a lot too, even when I’m trying to relax.
Has this worry been interfering with your work or daily life?

Yeah… it has, a bit. Work gets tense because I keep second-guessing decisions and pipeline reviews can drag or feel heavier than they should. And then when I get home, I’m just drained… I’m not really present with my husband, and I can be more reactive than I mean to be.
Do you worry a lot about things that have nothing to do with the sales division reorganization?

Yeah… it’s not only the reorg. My mind kind of jumps around—to launch numbers, whether someone on my team might leave, the mortgage, client renewals. Small delays can start feeling like they’re going to become something much bigger.
Does the worrying feel hard to control?
Yeah… it does. I’ll tell myself, like, “Brenda, you’ve made the plan, just leave it,” and then a few minutes later I’m right back in it. I’ll settle one worry and then three more kind of show up.
If the work reorganization were no longer an issue, do you think the worrying would still be there?

Yeah… I think it would. The reorg is part of it, but even without that, my mind would probably still go to the launch numbers, or whether someone on my team is going to leave, or the mortgage… things like that. Small delays just start to feel bigger than they probably are.
